title: Bug:[FRR][bgpd] running tcpdump on a BGP-neighbor interface triggers a full route re-download
author: yizhenzha
body: ### Is it platform specific generic ### Importance or Severity High ### Description of the bug Running `tcpdump` on an interface that has BGP neighbors triggers an unnecessary full route re-download, even without fib suppression enabled. Opening the capture puts the interface in promiscuous mode, which makes the kernel emit a netlink link message; zebra forwards it as a duplicate ZEBRA_INTERFACE_UP (oper up→up) even though nothing changed, and bgpd then re-evaluates the BGP nexthop cache (BNC) and re-installs/re-advertises every route via that interface. On a router with thousands of routes via an uplink this is a full-RIB re-install per tcpdump; with `bgp suppress-fib-pending` it floods the offload-confirmation path and delays BGP advertisement by multiple seconds. This is a regression: it was fixed by PR #21805 ### Steps to Reproduce **Preconditions**: a SONiC switch running BGP with many routes via an uplink (e.g. a T1 with several thousand routes over an uplink PortChannel), bgp suppress-fib-pending enabled (makes the re-download trivially visible via the offload flag; the route re-download itself happens regardless). **_method 1:_** Run community test on t1 topology: `bgp/test_bgp_suppress_fib.py::test_bgp_update_relay_latency`, which recently merged in https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/23390. The test’s [tcpdump sniffer step ](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/c93b8c4f0e722e45c1ddf90c2f6fee98f5ebcef8/tests/bgp/test_bgp_suppress_fib.py#L1659)triggered a full-RIB re-installs (~8k routes), which caused the latency of seconds during offload confirmation (orchagent → ROUTE_TABLE_RESPONSE_CHANNEL → fpmsyncd). The test itself will fail sincethe latency added **_method 2:_** manual reproduction on switch with T2 neighbour **1.Find the uplink interface toward an upstream (T2) BGP neighbor:** ```bash show ip bgp summary | grep T2 # pick a T2 neighbor IP, e.g. 10.0.0.1 show ip route 10.0.0.1 # -> "directly connected, PortChannelXXX" (the uplink iface) ``` **2.Confirm steady state — zero routes pending offload:** ```bash sudo vtysh -c "show ip route json" | python3 -c \ 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print("not_offloaded=",sum(1 for p in d.values() for r in p if r.get("installed") and not r.get("offloaded")))' # expect: not_offloaded= 0 ``` **3.Watch the pending-offload count (terminal 1) and start a capture on the uplink (terminal 2):** ```bash # terminal 1 — watch: while true; do date +%H:%M:%S | tr -d '\n'; \ sudo vtysh -c "show ip route json" | python3 -c \ 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(" not_offloaded=",sum(1 for p in d.values() for r in p if r.get("installed") and not r.get("offloaded")))'; \ sleep 1; done # terminal 2 — trigger (replace with your uplink ifa sudo timeout 5 tcpdump -ni PortChannelXXX 'tcp port 179' ``` **4.Observe: the instant tcpdump opens the interface (promiscuous mode), not_offloaded jumps from 0 → ~full RIB (~7,500 on this box) and drains over ~10s — i.e. tcpdump alone re-downloaded . No clear bgp, no config change.** Corroborating logs: ```bash # duplicate link-up from promiscuous mode: sudo grep -E "entered promiscuous mode|updatePortOpe /var/log/syslog # -> "Port PortChannelXXX oper state set from up to up" (a no-op up->up) # the route re-install storm: sudo docker exec swss sh -c \ "grep ROUTE_TABLE /var/log/swss/swss.rec | grep '|SET|' | tail -3000 | grep -oE '[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]' | uniq -c | tail" # -> a SET burst of thousands/sec right after the tcpdump ``` ### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior **Actual:** Running `tcpdump` on a BGP-neighbor / uplink interface causes a duplicate interface up→up event and a full route re-download. Reproduced on FRR 10.5.4: `tcpdump -ni PortChannel102 'tcp port 179'` on an idle box drove installed-but-not-offloaded routes from 0 to ~7,500 (the whole RIB via that uplink), draining over ~10s — with no clear/config/topology change. Both entering and leaving promiscuous mode fired it: kernel: PortChannel102: entered promiscuous mode orchagent: updatePortOperStatus: Port PortChannel102 oper state set from up to up -> swss.rec ROUTE_TABLE |SET burst up to 5120/s (BGP routes via the uplinks) **Expected:** `tcpdump` / promiscuous mode is a passive, local monitoring operation that does not change reachability or topology — it must NOT trigger any route update or download. The pending-offload count should stay 0 and there should be no route re-install. (Control: the same tcpdump on a non-BGP interface, e.g. eth0, causes no route churn.) ### Relevant log output ```shell 1. not_offloaded curve (the effect — tcpdump alone re-downloads the RIB) 02:03:13 not_offloaded=0 ← steady state 02:03:15 not_offloaded=0 ← tcpdump opened here 02:03:17 not_offloaded=7526 ← jumped: ~7.5k routes re-downloaded 02:03:19 not_offloaded=6136 02:03:20 not_offloaded=7076 ← tcpdump closed (adds a 2nd wave) 02:03:22 not_offloaded=6532 02:03:24 not_offloaded=1706 02:03:25 not_offloaded=387 02:03:27 not_offloaded=0 ← drained (~10s total) 2. syslog — the trigger (promiscuous → duplicate link-up → MTU re-set), on BOTH open and close # --- tcpdump OPEN --- 02:03:16.019 kernel: PortChannel102: entered promiscuous mode 02:03:16.019 kernel: Ethernet96: entered promiscuous mode (PC102 members) 02:03:16.019 kernel: Ethernet104: entered promiscuous mode 02:03:16.019 swss#portsyncd: onMsg: nlmsg type:16 key:Ethernet96 admin:1 oper:1 ... master:193 type:sx_netdev 02:03:16.019 swss#portsyncd: onMsg: nlmsg type:16 kr:1 ... type:team 02:03:16.022 swss#orchagent: updatePortOperStatus: Port PortChannel102 oper state set from up to up ← DUPLICATE up→up 02:03:16.024 swss#orchagent: setRouterIntfsMtu: Set102 MTU to 9100 # --- tcpdump CLOSE (5s later) — fires it AGAIN --- 02:03:20.019 kernel: PortChannel102: left promiscuous mode 02:03:20.019 kernel: Ethernet96/Ethernet104: left p 02:03:20.069 swss#orchagent: updatePortOperStatus: Port PortChannel102 oper state set from up to up ← DUPLICATE up→up 02:03:20.126 swss#orchagent: setRouterIntfsMtu: Set102 MTU to 9100 3. swss.rec — the route re-install storm ROUTE_TABLE |SET per second: 02:03:16 1146/s ← begins right after promiscuous-mode entry 02:03:17 1907/s 02:03:18 3072/s 02:03:19 2048/s 02:03:20 2048/s (tcpdump close adds more) 02:03:24 5120/s ← peak 02:03:25 5120/s 02:03:26 2059/s Sample re-installed routes (these are the T2-learned 02:03:24.046 ROUTE_TABLE:20c0:e658::/64 SET protocol:bgp nexthop:fc00::2,fc00::a,fc00::12,fc00::1a ifname:PortChannel102,105,108,111 02:03:24.053 ROUTE_TABLE:192.251.142.128/25 SET protocol:bgp nexthop:10.0.0.1,10.0.0.5,10.0.0.9,10.0.0.13 ifname:PortChannel102,105,108,111 02:03:24.301 ROUTE_TABLE:193.63.214.128/25 SET protocol:bgp nexthop:10.0.0.1,10.0.0.5,10.0.0.9,10.0.0.13 ifname:PortChannel102,105,108,111 02:03:24.517 ROUTE_TABLE:20c1:4da:0:80::/64 SET protocol:bgp nexthop:fc00::2,fc00::a,fc00::12,fc00::1a ifname:PortChannel102,105,108,111 4. offload-confirm churn (fpmsyncd RESPONSE_CHANNEL 02:03:16 received=322560 02:03:21 received=325632 02:03:26 received=350208 ← ~27.6k confirms pro ``` ### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport` ```shell ``` ### Attach files (if any) _No response_

comments.author: deepak-singhal0408
comments.body:
**Root cause — generic FRR (zebra + bgpd), two conditions both required:**

- **(A)** A `tcpdump` toggles `IFF_PROMISC`; zebra's `zebra_if_dplane_ifp_handling` doesn't filter promiscuity-only `RTM_NEWLINK` changes, so it sends a spurious `ZEBRA_INTERFACE_UP` to bgpd. (long-standing)
- **(B)** bgpd's `bgp_nht_ifp_table_handle` was broadened by upstream [`d1252ec`](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/commit/d1252ec2a6a) (2026-01-15) to re-evaluate **regular** single-nexthop BNCs on an interface-up — not just link-local ones. So on the spurious up, `evaluate_paths()` runs for every route via that interface → full re-advertise/re-install (both tcpdump open and close).

**When introduced:** condition (B) — [`d1252ec`](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/commit/d1252ec2a6a), first released in **FRR 10.5.4**. In 10.5.1 and earlier, only link-local nexthops were matched, so regular-nexthop routes were untouched and the symptom didn't occur.

**Affected branches (by FRR pin):**

| SONiC branch | FRR pin | (B) present? | Affected? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `master` | 10.5.4 | ✅ ([`d1252ec`](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/commit/d1252ec2a6a)) | ✅ **Yes** |
| `202511` | 10.4.1 | ❌ | ❌ No |
| ≤ 202505 | ≤ 10.4.x | ❌ | ❌ No |

**Upstream fix:** [FRRouting/frr#20181](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/20181) (commit [`257edcc`](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/commit/257edcc948), merged 2026-01-07) fixes (A) at the source — when `change_flags == IFF_PROMISC` it updates `ifp->flags` and returns early, suppressing the notification. It currently lands in **10.6.0+ only** and is **not** on `stable/10.5`, so frr-10.5.4 lacks it.

**Quick fix:** backport [FRRouting/frr#20181](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/20181) onto frr-10.5.4 → [sonic-buildimage#28043](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/28043). No `202511` backport needed (10.4.1 predates [`d1252ec`](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/commit/d1252ec2a6a)). Since the fix is in 10.6.0+ only, SONiC must carry this patch on the 10.5.x line; requesting an upstream `stable/10.5` backport of [FRRouting/frr#20181](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/20181) would let the carried patch be dropped on a future 10.5.x bump.

linkedPullRequests.title: [sonic-frr]: suppress full BGP route re-download when tcpdump toggles interface promiscuity
linkedPullRequests.author: deepak-singhal0408
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/28026

On a BGP-enabled port or PortChannel, running `tcpdump` (or opening any `AF_PACKET` socket) toggles `IFF_PROMISC`. FRR 10.5.4 zebra does not filter a promiscuity-only netlink change in `zebra_if_dplane_ifp_handling`, so it emits a spurious `ZEBRA_INTERFACE_UP`. bgpd then re-evaluates every nexthop tracked via that interface and re-advertises/re-installs the full RIB (thousands of routes, ~10 s of control-plane churn). A routine packet capture on a production device should never trigger a routing storm.

Root cause: the netlink `ifi_change` mask carrying `IFF_PROMISC` (`0x100`) is not inspected before the interface is treated as having changed operational state.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

Add SONiC FRR patch `0115`, a backport of upstream [FRRouting/frr PR 20181](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/20181) (commit `257edcc948e0179c75933cdb862fe1ac4ac14085`, "zebra: Update promiscuity flag silently without route resets").

The patch plumbs the netlink `ifi_change` mask through the dplane (`dplane_ctx_set/get_ifp_change_flags`) and, in `zebra_if_dplane_ifp_handling`, skips the routing notification when promiscuity is the **only** changed flag (`change_flags == IFF_PROMISC`, exact match on the masked value). The interface flags are still updated, so `show interface` reflects the correct PROMISC state.

PR scope — patch-based, **no submodule pointer change**:
- `src/sonic-frr/patch/0115-zebra-Update-promiscuity-flag-silently-without-route.patch`
- `src/sonic-frr/patch/series`

Porting note: upstream's `frrtrace(... if_dplane_ifp_handling_new ...)` tracepoint does not exist on `frr-10.5.4` and is omitted; the suppression logic is otherwise verbatim. Upstream PR 20181 is not yet in a released `stable/10.5`, hence the SONiC patch.

#### How to verify it

- **Patch apply:** full series `0001`–`0115` applies cleanly on a pristine `frr-10.5.4` tree (0 rejects).
- **Compile:** `frr_10.5.4-sonic-0_amd64.deb` builds clean with the patch applied (and the `docker-fpm-frr` container assembles).
- **Functional (KVM t1-lag, cEOS neighbors, before/after container swap):** Trigger (both runs): `tcpdump -ni PortChannel102 'tcp port 179'` (open+close) on a LAG uplink. DUT had 24 BGP sessions Established, RIB ~12.8k.

  | Metric | BEFORE (unfixed FRR 10.5.4) | AFTER (patch 0115) |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | swss.rec `ROUTE_TABLE` ops | **25,512** | **0** |
  | bgpd `eval path` lines | 10,059 | 0 |
  | zebra `ZEBRA_INTERFACE_UP PortChannel102` | yes | no |
  | zebra `PROMISC-only update … no routing notification` (fix firing) | n/a | yes |
  | RIB ebgp routes (steady) | 6,427 | 6,427 |

BEFORE: the promisc toggle produced a spurious `ZEBRA_INTERFACE_UP`, bgpd re-evaluated the paths, and the full RIB was re-downloaded (25,512 `ROUTE_TABLE` ops). AFTER: the same toggle produced **zero** route ops, zero path re-evaluation, and no `ZEBRA_INTERFACE_UP`; `not_offloaded` stayed 0. `ip monitor` confirmed the netlink delta is `promiscuity` only (`ifi_change == IFF_PROMISC`, `0x100`), not allmulti.
- **sonic-mgmt:** `bgp/test_bgp_suppress_fib.py::test_bgp_update_relay_latency` → **PASS**.

#### Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)

<!-- Not requesting a backport in this PR: the fix is specific to the frr-10.5.4 tree pinned on master and was validated on master only. A backport to a release branch on an earlier FRR would require a separately authored/validated port. -->

- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [ ] 202605

#### Tested branch (Please provide the tested image version)

- [x] master — base image `sonic-vs` build `1145536` (master, 2026-06-22) with the patched `docker-fpm-frr` container swapped in.

#### Description for the changelog

[sonic-frr] zebra: suppress full BGP route re-download on interface promiscuity-only changes (tcpdump toggling `IFF_PROMISC`).

#### Link to config_db schema for YANG module changes

N/A — no CONFIG_DB schema or YANG changes.

comments.body:
### 202605 branch verification ✅ (cherry-pick request)

Verified this fix on the **202605 release branch** with a matched A/B on a KVM `t1-lag` testbed (vlab-03), 202605 nightly `202605.1157773-9c84048a4` (FRR 10.5.4, Debian 13/trixie) — BGP 24/24, ARISTA01T2 (10.0.0.1) on PortChannel102 = 6371 prefixes. The 202605 nightly is pre-fix (unfixed baseline); the container image is the only variable.

**Trigger:** `sudo timeout 3 tcpdump -ni PortChannel102 'tcp port 179'` (promisc open+close).
**Signal:** ROUTE_TABLE ops in `/var/log/swss/swss.rec` during the trigger window.

| Build | tcpdump promisc toggle on PortChannel102 | ROUTE_TABLE ops |
|---|---|---|
| **UNFIXED** 202605 nightly | full RIB re-download | **25,488** |
| **FIXED** (this PR's patch 0115, container-swap) | silent, no reset | **0** |

`regression_confirmed = true`, `fix_confirmed = true` on 202605 — the promisc toggle drives a whole-RIB re-download on the unfixed nightly (25,488 ops), and **0** ops with the promiscuity-silent patch. The FRR pin is identical master↔202605 and the patch cherry-picks cleanly. Requesting cherry-pick approval to 202605.
